title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
abstract: arXiv:2610.30678v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets are insufficient for this, as they are either limited in scale or already saturated. We therefore construct six new safety datasets of sufficient size and difficulty. translated_abstract: 安全探针是在模型激活值上训练的、用于实时监控语言模型的标准工具。每当发布新模型或需要监控新的危害领域时，探针都必须重新训练，这需要新的标签以及探针架构的选择。然而，无论是模型还是标签都无法预先告诉我们最终探针的性能如何，要弄清这一点需要训练并比较多种探针配置。在本文中，我们探讨是否可以仅凭模型规模和标签数量来提前预测探针的性能。现有的安全数据集不足以支持这一研究，因为它们要么规模有限，要么已经饱和。因此，我们构建了六个规模足够大、难度足够高的新安全数据集。在这些数据集上，我们在来自五个模型家族的20个基础模型上训练了两种探针架构，每个模型使用32到10⁶个标签。我们使用探针误差来衡量性能……
tldr: 本文通过构建六个新安全数据集、在20个基础模型上以不同标签规模训练探针，首次提出了可依据模型规模和标签数量提前预测安全探针性能的缩放定律。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes scaling laws for safety probes, showing that probe performance can be predicted in advance from model size and the number of training labels.
